extra.message: SQL injection via id parameter — Attacker can read arbitrary DB data (e.g. admin password) via UNION/blind SQLi, fully compromising the credential store. [verified: `params["id"]` is concatenated directly into the SQL string passed to cursor.execute with no parameterization; results are reflected, enabling UNION/blind SQLi to read the admin password.]

Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads (object param) — Remote code execution / OS command execution on the server. [verified: `params["object"]` is passed to pickle.loads on fully attacker-controlled bytes, enabling __reduce__-based RCE; the CASES demo even ships a system() pickle payload.]

OS command injection via domain parameter — Attacker executes arbitrary OS commands on the server. [verified: `params["domain"]` is concatenated into 'nslookup '+domain and run with subprocess.run(shell=True); metacharacters inject arbitrary OS commands.]

Remote/local file inclusion leading to code execution via include param — Remote code execution: attacker hosts a payload and the server fetches and exec()s it. [verified: `params["include"]` is read from a local file or urllib URL and the bytes passed directly to exec(), giving remote code execution.]

SQL injection / authentication bypass on /login — Attacker bypasses authentication and logs in as any user including admin, obtaining a session. [verified: At /login the `password` param is concatenated unsanitized into the WHERE clause (only username is stripped via re.sub), allowing classic `' OR '1'='1`-style auth bypass.]

DOM-based XSS via location.hash 'lang=' parameter — Arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser session, enabling session/cookie theft, credential phishing, and full account/page takeover via a crafted link. [verified: HTML_PREFIX (line 12) inline script reads document.location.hash, takes the substring after 'lang=', and passes it through only decodeURIComponent into document.write() with no escaping, so /#lang=<script> executes attacker JS in the victim's DOM.]

Reflected XSS via v parameter — Attacker executes arbitrary JavaScript in victims' browsers (session/credential theft). [verified: `params["v"]` is substituted into HTML output via re.sub with no HTML escaping, reflecting attacker markup directly into the page.]

Path traversal / arbitrary local file disclosure via path param — Attacker reads arbitrary files readable by the server process, including source and secrets. [verified: `params["path"]` without '://' is opened via os.path.abspath with no traversal/whitelist check, allowing arbitrary local file disclosure (e.g. /etc/passwd, dsvw.py).]

SSRF via path parameter — Attacker reaches internal network services (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:631) and exfiltrates their responses. [verified: When `params["path"]` contains '://' it is fetched via urllib.request.urlopen with no host validation, allowing SSRF to loopback/internal services.]

XML External Entity (XXE) injection via xml param — Attacker reads local files (file:///etc/passwd) and performs SSRF via remote entities. [verified: `params["xml"]` is parsed with lxml XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False), enabling XXE local file read and SSRF.]

XPath injection via name parameter — Attacker manipulates the XPath query to extract data (e.g. admin password via blind boolean XPath). [verified: `params["name"]` is interpolated directly into the XPath string `.//user[name/text()='%s']`, allowing XPath injection to extract data.]

Stored SQL injection and stored XSS via comment parameter — Attacker injects SQL into the comments store and persists XSS payloads executed in other users' browsers. [verified: `params["comment"]` is inserted via string formatting into the INSERT (stored SQLi) with no escaping; the SQLi class is confirmed at line 50.]

Stored XSS via comment display — Attacker-supplied JavaScript persists in the comment store and runs in the browser of every visitor of the comments page, enabling session/cookie theft, credential phishing, and arbitrary actions as the victim. [verified: Stored comments are rendered back via `%s % _` with no HTML escaping at line 53, so persisted `

Path traversal / arbitrary local file read via include parameter — Disclosure (and execution as Python) of arbitrary files readable by the server process, exposing source, secrets, and system files. [verified: Line 57 calls open(params['include'],'rb') for include values without '://' with no traversal sanitization, so /?include=../../../../etc/passwd reads arbitrary files which are then exec'd as Python.]

SSRF via include parameter URL fetch — Server-side requests to internal/cloud-metadata/internal-only services, enabling internal network reconnaissance and access to otherwise unreachable endpoints; combined with exec it also enables remote code execution. [verified: Line 57 calls urllib.request.urlopen(params['include']) for any value containing '://' with no host/scheme allowlist, letting an attacker force server-side requests to internal/cloud-metadata endpoints; the response is then exec'd, escalating to RCE.]

HTTP response splitting / header injection via charset param — Attacker injects arbitrary response headers/body (e.g. fake login form), enabling phishing/XSS. [verified: `params.get("charset")` is placed unsanitized into the Content-Type header; CR/LF in the value splits the response and injects headers/body (CASES demo confirms %0D%0A payload).]

Denial of service via unbounded size parameter — Attacker exhausts server memory/CPU with a single request (e.g. size=9999999), causing DoS. [verified: At line 46 both the repetition count and string multiplier come from unbounded int(params["size"]), building a size^2 in-memory string and exhausting memory.]

Open redirect via redir parameter — Attacker crafts links that redirect victims to phishing/malicious sites under the trusted host. [verified: `params["redir"]` is placed into a meta refresh url with no target validation, enabling open redirect to arbitrary sites.]

JSONP/reflected XSS via callback parameter — Attacker executes arbitrary JavaScript and exfiltrates the user data returned by /users.json. [verified: `params["callback"]` is concatenated into the /users.json body unescaped and served, executing as script when included; same JSONP sink as idx 20.]

Weak/predictable session token generation — Attacker may predict/brute-force session identifiers and hijack authenticated sessions. [verified: SESSIONID is built with random.sample over the non-cryptographic Mersenne-Twister PRNG, making session tokens predictable.]

Insecure session cookie flags and missing brute-force protection — Session cookies are exposed to script/MITM and login can be brute-forced, easing account takeover. [verified: The session cookie is set via meta Set-Cookie with no HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite flags, and /login has no rate-limiting/CSRF protection on the state-changing GET route.]

Sensitive information disclosure via full traceback in responses — Attacker gains source paths and internal logic aiding further exploitation. [verified: The except handler returns traceback.format_exc() in the HTTP body with INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, leaking stack traces and file paths.]

Security header disabling browser XSS protection — Disables a browser-side mitigation, increasing likelihood of successful XSS exploitation. [verified: The finally block explicitly sends X-XSS-Protection: 0, disabling the browser-side XSS mitigation and compounding the XSS sinks.]
